review_output: {"summary":"Based on the supplied text only (nothing executed), both prior MAJOR findings are resolved; this is not an approval of the whole Goal. (1) MAJOR old-scope UPDATE fence: RESOLVED. The revision trigger only records events for the NEW scope. But `wp20_metric_scope_update` (`LiveMetricRegistration_scope_immutable`, BEFORE UPDATE) rejects any change to id, vendorId, liveId or versionId with 23514, and the registration guard also blocks identity changes. A row can't move scope, so the old scope can't miss its event. The runtime probe got 23514. One weakness remains: it checks only the SQLSTATE (see NIT below). (2) MAJOR TRUNCATE bypass: RESOLVED for `LiveMetricRegistration`. The new `LiveMetricRegistration_no_truncate` trigger runs BEFORE TRUNCATE for each statement. PostgreSQL also fires TRUNCATE triggers on tables reached through CASCADE, and the real TRUNCATE CASCADE probe of the source tables plus `LiveMetricRegistration` passes. One related gap: the revision ledger table has no truncate protection shown (MINOR below). (3) Prior MINOR error-mapping tests: RESOLVED. There is now a real two-connection race between the revision read and the INSERT that returns `source_changed` with no proof row, plus unit tests for the dedicated guard, an unrelated 23514, a 55P03 that reuses the guard message, and an audit failure that never reaches the writer. (4) Prior MINOR ledger retention on Live-only delete: STILL OPEN, as you stated. The projection-delete lifecycle test (delete → unknown, recreate → unknown, re-audit → complete) correctly shows that a deleted and recreated projection does not bring an old proof back.
